BHARTIHEXA: Airtel-brand telecom operator for Rajasthan and the North-East (Bharti Airtel owns 70%). Q1 FY27 revenue +10.9% to ₹2,510cr, PAT +23.2% to ₹482cr, EBITDA margin up ~100bps to 54.8%. ARPU rose to ₹259 from ₹246; data traffic +30.5%; the Homes/broadband segment grew 61.4% YoY. Note the disconnect: operations are compounding nicely but the stock is down ~13% over a year and trades near 42x, so a lot was already priced in.
BAJAJHLDNG: Bajaj group holding company — stakes in Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Auto and Maharashtra Scooters. Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT ₹2,708cr, which reads as −22% YoY only because Q1 FY26 carried a ₹1,522cr one-off gain from a Bajaj Finserv block deal; strip that out and underlying PAT grew ~28%. Share of associate profits rose 24.6% to ₹2,359cr. Watch item: RBI approval pending on re-categorisation as an unregistered Core Investment Company. Standard holding-company caveat — you own the underlying via a discount, and the discount can widen.
VGUARD: Kochi-based electricals and consumer durables (stabilisers, water heaters, wires, kitchen appliances). Excellent quarter: Q1 FY27 revenue +23.5% to ₹1,811cr against 14-15% full-year guidance, PAT +76% to ₹130cr, EBITDA margin up 210bps to 10.5%. Net cash improved sharply to ₹670cr from ₹155cr. Growth was helped by a favourable summer and pricing actions that offset copper inflation, so some of this is seasonal rather than run-rate. South region grew 36.7% vs 12% non-South.
DEEPAKNTR: Specialty chemicals — phenolics and advanced intermediates. Best quarter on record: Q1 FY27 revenue +35% to ₹2,592cr, PAT +207% to ₹345cr, EBITDA margin doubling to 21% from 11%. Phenolics did the heavy lifting with record segment EBIT of ₹418cr at 24% margins. Debt-to-equity a comfortable 0.27x, and the board approved ₹2,500cr for a 240 KTA Bisphenol A plant to deepen integration. Caveat: this is a cyclical spread business — the margin doubling reflects favourable phenol-benzene spreads as much as execution, and advanced intermediates still faces raw-material pressure.
HINDCOPPER: Government-owned Miniratna copper miner, holds all operating copper mining leases in India. Q1 FY27 revenue +81% to ₹937cr, PAT +162% to ₹352cr, EBITDA margin 54%. Two caveats worth weighing: sequentially profit actually fell 21% from Q4 FY26, so the YoY figure flatters; and auditors flagged governance gaps — no independent directors since Nov 2024 and no woman director since Mar 2025. Targets 4.7mt mine production in FY27. Reported talks with Codelco on Chilean supply are early-stage and unconfirmed.
PAKKA: Formerly Yash Pakka — compostable and moulded-fibre food packaging (Chuk brand), based in Ayodhya. Q1 FY27 rebounded in both revenue and profit after a sharp FY26 profit decline. Two real red flags: the auditor issued a qualified opinion over uncertainty on a major overseas project, and the board has approved USD 1mn to restart US operations. Small company — revenue in the ₹100-500cr band with roughly flat multi-year revenue CAGR and negative EBITDA CAGR. Treat the momentum as sentiment-driven; the accounts do not yet support it.
KHAICHEM: Single super phosphate and sulphuric acid maker across MP, UP, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. Q1 FY27 PAT ₹10.9cr — up sharply sequentially but down 49% YoY from ₹21.4cr, on revenue of ₹221cr (−6% YoY). The segment split is the real story: fertilisers collapsed to ₹112cr from ₹187cr while chemicals grew to ₹110cr from ₹68cr. So the business is mid-rotation between segments rather than simply growing. Micro-cap, thinly traded.
PTCIL: PTC Industries — titanium and superalloy precision castings for aerospace and defence, via subsidiary Aerolloy. Q1 FY27 revenue +98% to ₹192cr and PAT +466% to ₹29cr, EBITDA margin expanding 954bps to 27.5%. Contracts with Airbus, BrahMos and the MoD point to a shift from component to systems supplier, and the UK subsidiary Trac Precision has stabilised. The catch is valuation: ~₹28,500cr market cap on ₹697cr trailing revenue and ₹126cr profit, trading at roughly 19x book, no dividend. Also note revenue and profit both fell sequentially from Q4 FY26.
MAXESTATES: NCR real-estate developer (Noida and Gurugram), wellbeing-led LiveWell/WorkWell positioning. The headline is pre-sales: ~₹1,093cr in Q1 FY27, over 5x YoY, with 487 units sold against 43 a year ago, and ₹491cr collected. ICRA assigned a first-time A+ issuer rating. Commercial portfolio is 100% leased generating ₹150cr+ annual rent. But reported P&L is thin and going the other way — Q1 FY27 PAT fell 30% YoY to ₹8.35cr on revenue of ₹52cr, with EBITDA down 42%. That gap is normal for developers, where pre-sales convert to revenue only on construction milestones, but it means the accounts will lag the story for several quarters. GDV pipeline ₹16,150cr+.
UNIONBANK: PSU bank. Q1 FY27 standalone PAT +29.5% to ₹5,332cr, gross NPA down to 2.65% from 3.52% YoY, net NPA 0.47%, capital adequacy 18.46%, provision coverage ~95%. The catch is growth: deposit growth of ~3.5% badly trails the 8-9% guidance and credit growth of 12.5% is below target, so profit is coming from asset-quality improvement more than expansion.
CASTROLIND: Near debt-free lubricants leader, 51% owned by bp; ~43% ROE, ~4.7% dividend yield, 109% payout. Q2 CY26 (Jun quarter) was excellent: revenue +25% to ₹1,871cr, PAT +43% to ₹348cr, EBITDA +41% to ₹494cr, interim dividend of ₹6.25 nearly doubled YoY. Two caveats. Management itself flagged that part of the margin came from consuming cheaper inventory carried from an earlier peak — a one-off, though they say profitability grew healthily even excluding it — and stayed cautious on H2 given commodity inflation and an uneven monsoon. Separately, bp is selling 65% of Castrol's global lubricants business to Stonepeak (~USD 10bn EV), expected to close end-2026; no financial impact yet, but the ownership change is a live overhang. Stock is down ~9% over a year despite the earnings, and trades ~9.7x book.
JUBLFOOD: Operates Domino's, Popeyes and Hong's Kitchen; 3,712 stores. Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue +14.1% to ₹2,570cr but PAT only +6% to ₹100cr, EBITDA margin flat at 19.6%. The split matters more than the headline: Popeyes like-for-like sales grew 45% (third straight quarter above 40%, revenue +97%), while core Domino's India LFL was just 2.5% against 11.6% a year ago. So growth is coming from a small, fast brand while the large mature one has stalled. Management guides 5-7% Domino's LFL for FY27 with recovery from Q2. Broker views diverge sharply — Jefferies Buy at ₹650, HSBC Hold at ₹500. Debt-to-equity 0.76, capex ₹750-900cr, and the stock trades near 88x against a sector ~62x. Expensive for the growth currently being delivered.
PETRONET: PSU-promoted LNG importer (GAIL, IOC, BPCL, ONGC), handles ~75% of India's LNG imports. Q1 FY27 standalone PAT +33% to ₹1,133cr — but read the composition carefully. Volumes actually *fell* 5.9% to 207 TBTU, and Dahej utilisation dropped to 66% from 92%, partly because expansion raised nameplate capacity to 22.5 MMTPA. Profit rose on ₹301cr of trading gains and ₹193cr of inventory gains from the spot-vs-contract price gap; Nomura calculates that adjusted for those, PAT was 3% *below* estimate. Revenue fell 53% YoY as missing Qatar volumes were replaced by tolling arrangements that book only the tolling fee. Also note: PBT declined sequentially from ₹1,795cr, auditors flagged ₹661cr of use-or-pay dues recoverability, Kochi still runs at 23% utilisation, and five-year sales growth is a poor 10.8%. A good quarter driven substantially by trading, not throughput.
POKARNA: Hyderabad-based exporter of engineered quartz (Quantra brand, Bretonstone licence) and granite; quartz is ~93% of revenue. Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT +50.5% YoY to ₹42.6cr and +66% sequentially, on revenue +10.8% to ₹189cr, with EBITDA margin expanding to 35.9% from 32.1%. The granite segment turned positive (₹3.2cr) after a prior-year loss, reducing single-segment dependence. Context is essential though: this is a recovery off a bad base — FY26 consolidated profit fell 57% to ₹80.6cr, and Q3 FY26 saw revenue drop 40% YoY. The business is export-led and therefore geared to US housing demand and freight rates, neither of which it controls. Screener flags possible interest capitalisation and debtor days rising from 76 to 92. Promoter holding 56.7%, dividend negligible.
MUKKA: Mangaluru fish-meal and fish-oil maker for aqua, poultry and pet feed; ~87% of revenue is export across 20+ countries. Q1 FY27 looks spectacular — consolidated revenue +187% to ₹475cr and PAT +1,073% to ₹18.6cr, EBITDA margin 10.1%. Treat that with real caution. The base quarter was tiny (₹1.6cr PAT), so the percentage is arithmetic rather than transformation, and ₹18.6cr on a ₹817cr market cap is still thin. More seriously, independent analysis flags weak earnings quality: operating cash flow has been negative in most years and deeply negative in FY26, free cash flow consistently negative, and leverage rose again on a large FY26 debt increase. One tracker notes profit not converting to cash with receivables growing faster than sales. Average ROCE ~8.8% is modest, and at least one house rates it Sell. Also mid-acquisition (51% of Delta Marine, a stake in a loss-making waste-management firm) and withdrew a planned ₹75cr NCD issue. Momentum is real; the accounts are not yet confirming it.
GODREJAGRO: Diversified agri-business (animal feed, crop protection, oil palm, dairy, foods). Q1 FY27 is a case of good top line, weak bottom line: consolidated sales +10% to ₹2,852cr but EBITDA −9% to ₹255cr, margin compressing to 8.9% from 10.8%, and PAT −14% to ₹128cr. Animal Nutrition was the bright spot — cattle feed volumes +15%, segment result +36% — and Oil Palm revenue +28.9% on better CPO realisations and an improved 18.8% extraction ratio. Crop Care fell 17.2% on a delayed monsoon. Genuine positives: net working capital days improved to 21 from 31, ROCE ~20%, Astec reached EBITDA breakeven, ICRA reaffirmed AA/A1+, and India's first integrated oil palm complex opened in Telangana. Watch items: CFO transition (S. Varadaraj superannuating, Ravishankar A. from 1 Oct), and management deferring precise FY27 guidance until after Q2. The stock fell ~4% on results despite a slight EPS beat.
LICI: India's largest life insurer and the cleanest fundamental story in this week's list. Q1 FY27 PAT +22.8% to ₹13,492cr, but the more meaningful number is Value of New Business +61.3% to ₹3,136cr with VNB margin expanding 750bps to 22.9% from 15.4%. That reflects a real mix shift — non-par products now 32.5% of individual APE versus 30.3% a year ago, with non-par savings APE +59% and protection +44%. Solvency improved to 2.42 from 2.17; AUM ₹59.4 lakh crore. Three honest caveats: headline growth is modest (total APE only +8.2%, premium +6.75%, and policies sold up just 2.1%), so profit is coming from margin not volume; first-year premium market share slipped to 60.10% from 63.51% as private competition bites; and 61st-month persistency weakened to 61.12% from 63.85%.
HINDOILEXP: Small Chennai-based oil and gas explorer (~₹2,060cr market cap). Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41-45% YoY to ₹124cr consolidated, but profit collapsed: standalone PAT −74% to ₹12.5cr and consolidated net profit down to ₹6.2cr from ₹43.9cr. Worse, standalone other income of ₹19.4cr included one-offs — an ₹8cr escrow release and a ₹2cr insurance claim — meaning operating profit was thinner still. Operationally B-80 produced only 605 BOEPD and a dispute with HPCL over a ~417,000-barrel cargo containing organic chlorides is unresolved, with the oil being resold to third parties into late 2026. Dirok and Kharsang are improving, and FY27 capex is USD 45mn with three new B-80 wells in Q4. Also note: the company was fined by both exchanges for delayed FY26 results amid management and auditor changes, pays no dividend despite repeated profits, and Screener flags a low tax rate. Genuinely high-risk.
RENUKA: Wilmar-controlled sugar and ethanol producer, and the weakest balance sheet on either list — flag this one hard. Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹2,120cr (+5.5%) with a consolidated net loss of ₹252cr, only marginally better than the ₹260cr loss a year ago; the standalone loss actually widened slightly. The structural problem: standalone net worth is **negative ₹1,494cr**, consolidated current liabilities exceed current assets by roughly ₹3,691cr, and debt is around ₹5,566cr. FY26 closed with a ₹792cr net loss. Solvency rests on parent Wilmar International's continued liquidity support. The distillery segment is the one bright spot (revenue up sharply to ₹474cr) and India's ethanol blending push is a real tailwind, but this is a turnaround bet dependent on policy and a parent's balance sheet, not a compounding business. Peers like Balrampur Chini are far better capitalised.
BALUFORGE: Belgaum-based precision forging and machining, pivoting hard into defence and aerospace. Q1 FY27 revenue +29% to ₹300.7cr and PAT +15.9% to ₹66.1cr, with sequential revenue +14%. Strategically busy: maiden US aerospace order from Alpha Aircraft Systems, a five-year MoU with a NATO-affiliated entity for large-calibre shells, a ₹100cr confirmed order for 155mm ERFB shells, and an ICRA upgrade to A-(Stable)/A2+. The caution is in the margin trend and the funding. EBITDA margin fell to 28.2% from 31.0% and PAT margin to 21.7% from 24.3%, because finance costs more than doubled to ₹46cr and depreciation rose 96.5%. The board has approved a USD 60mn FCCB issue and a borrowing-limit increase to ₹1,000cr (EGM 4 Sept) — meaningful dilution and leverage ahead. Auditors also flagged a related-party property purchase and ongoing tax proceedings, and promoter holding fell 0.88% in the quarter. Note that some outlets misreport the figures in millions as crore; revenue is ₹300.7cr, not ₹3,007cr.
JAYSREETEA: Micro-cap (₹266cr) B.K. Birla group company in tea, sugar and P&K fertilisers. Q1 FY27 revenue +8.6% to ₹203cr with the standalone net loss narrowing to just ₹6.18 lakh from ₹94.3 lakh; consolidated loss ₹59.4 lakh. Tea carried the quarter with a ₹10.3cr segment profit, offsetting losses in Sugar and Fertilisers. Two things to weigh seriously: **auditors issued a qualified opinion** over non-provisioning of income tax, with the company citing seasonality and deferring provisions to year-end — so the reported loss is understated by an unquantified amount. And the trailing picture is poor: −₹22cr profit on ₹946cr revenue, low interest coverage, and five-year sales growth of just 3%. The business is also inherently seasonal, so a single quarter tells you little. Thinly traded.
ORIENTCER: Ashapura-group specialty ceramics maker (calcined and fused alumina, refractories, ceramic proppants) at Porbandar; ₹519cr market cap. The Q1 FY27 story is portfolio simplification rather than earnings: the board completed disposal of the Power Division, now reported as discontinued operations, and sold seven windmills via slump sale for ₹16.45cr. Recent trend was improving — Q4 FY26 net sales +16.2% to ₹98.2cr with net profit +63.2% to ₹5.7cr — and exports have scaled to about ₹88cr. Debt has been reduced and dividend payout maintained at ~21.7%. The clear negative is returns: ROE averaged just 6.25% over three years on ₹405cr revenue and ₹26cr profit, which is thin for a capital-intensive manufacturer. Ashapura International raised its stake to 8.35% in March. Small, illiquid, and the divestments make year-on-year comparisons messy for the next few quarters.
SEAMECLTD: Offshore marine services — diving support vessels and vessel charter for oil and gas. Market cap ~₹4,159cr, up strongly over the past year; trailing revenue ₹952cr and profit ₹254cr, promoter holding 72.7%. Recent developments: a USD 9.42mn diving agreement with HAL Offshore, and vessel SEAMEC SWORDFISH off-hired from 30 July for planned maintenance, which will dent the coming quarter's utilisation. Caution: reported quarterly figures differ materially across secondary sources for this name — verify against the company filing before relying on any single quarter. Trades at roughly 3x book and the effective tax rate looks unusually low. Revenue is inherently lumpy since it depends on vessel day-rates and contract timing rather than a steady order book.
